fig1_shaft_power_vs_rpm.svg: Shaft power $\dot W=\tau\omega$ (shaft_power, with rpm_to_rad_s converting rev/min to rad/s) is linear in speed at fixed torque. The same 12.6 kW can be delivered as 40 N$\cdot$m at 3000 rpm or as 20 N$\cdot$m at 6000 rpm — the trade a gearbox exists to make. Power is a RATE, not an amount: it says nothing about how much energy has moved until it is multiplied by a duration.
fig2_energy_from_power.svg: Holding power constant, the energy transferred is $\dot W\Delta t$ (energy_from_power) — a straight line whose slope IS the power. Two minutes at 3 kW moves 360 kJ, the same energy a 500 W trickle would take twelve minutes to deliver. The marked point closes the loop: feeding that energy back through power_from_work recovers the original 1500 W, which is the arithmetic identity the two helpers are meant to satisfy.
